WHAT IT SHOWS.
For one checkpoint (and optionally a second, for comparison), one study and one label: every slot of the bag with the label's attention weight and a Grad-CAM overlay.
The CAM is scripts/gradcam.py's, and the numbers match (selftest;
pinned in the smoke suite).
T074 showed it tracks the trained weights, not the input statistics.
The two normalisations are gradcam.py's two readings:
slice: each slice scaled to its own peak -- WHERE the evidence sits, given this slice is looked at at all;
bag: every slice on one scale for the label -- WHAT drove the logit, with attention and localisation multiplied together.
WHAT IT IS NOT.
An instrument, never a result.
Per-study pictures cannot support a column-level claim, and a defect screen can find something wrong but never confirm something right (gradcam.py's docstring;
A checkpoint trained with --train-gold has seen the gold labels, so its gold p is in-sample, and the page says so.

One forward per study, then ONE batched autograd.grad gives all twelve labels' channel gradients: measured 0.17 s on CPU, against 3.6-4.4 s PER LABEL for a full backward().
The encoder is frozen and the hooked activation is re-rooted as a leaf, so the graph behind it is never kept and the backward stops at the layer Grad-CAM needs.

A CUDA context held by an idle viewer makes gpu_queue.sh read the card as busy, and a queued fold then defers indefinitely.

LayerCAM is what the page shows. At the layer we hook, global average pooling follows, so every channel's gradient is constant across space.
Grad-CAM then sums w_c A_c over channels and lets a channel that pushes the logit DOWN cancel one that pushes it up;
LayerCAM keeps only the positive contributions.
Measured on armC_fold0 and one gold study's ACL, that moved edge_mass from 0.370 -- a flat map's 0.36, i.e. no localisation at all -- to 0.161.

GradCAM stays wired as the anchor, not as a choice. It is the one method the library and gradcam.py both implement, so selftest and the smoke suite compare them (8.0e-06 apart, with bit-identical activations, gradients and raw maps).
That equality is what says the library is reading OUR model correctly before LayerCAM's output is believed.
The other seven the library offers are not wired, and the measurements are in T097: HiResCAM and XGradCAM reduce to Grad-CAM here (correlation +1.000, same constant-gradient argument);
EigenCAM ignores the label;
the Eigen methods' sign is arbitrary;
RandomCAM is a weaker version of T074's control;
ScoreCAM and AblationCAM cost one masked forward per channel, which is 1,408 forwards of a 36-slice bag per label on CPU.
One line under the page's title, so what is on screen is never in doubt.
The library calls model(input_tensor) on a 4-D tensor and reads its width and height off the last two axes.
A 5-D tensor would be taken for a 3-D volume.
So the bag's slots stand in as the batch (S, 3, H, W), and mask and meta are bound here.

logits (L,) depends on act (S, C, h, w).
Row j of the identity as the grad output gives d logit_j / d act, which is exactly what gradcam.CAM gets from logits[j].backward();

WHAT IT WRITES, and why it is 148 GB and not the 49.4 GB T121 registered.
make_bag returns images of shape (N, 3, 384, 384) -- PRE-FORMED TRIPLETS, not a 76-slice single-channel volume.
T121's cost table assumed the latter.
Measured before this was written: windows inside a slot do NOT generally overlap (w0[1] != w1[0] for slots 1-4;
only slot 5 does), so they are STRIDED across the slot's span, the triplets are ATOMIC, and no compact slice volume can reconstruct them. 4,407 x 76 x 3 x 384^2 = 148.2 GB.
LAYOUT.
One fixed (76, 3, 384, 384) uint8 block per study, windows placed at their slot's offset, plus a (76,) uint8 validity mask.

The budgets (20,12,12,8,16,8) are dicom_bag.SLOT_BUDGETS and the offsets are their cumulative sum, so a window's slot is recoverable from its index alone -- which is what the T119 window rule needs and what the 0942's all-ones mask destroys.
WORKERS WRITE THEIR OWN ROW.
Each opens the memmap r+ and writes only its study's slice, so the rows never overlap and nothing is pickled back through the pool.
Returning 11 MB of pixels per study through IPC would move 148 GB through a pipe to write 148 GB to disk.
